<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
$\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}f(n)/n=m_1$. Moreover $f(n)\ge m_1n$ for every $n\ge1$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:num}
$0.22936\,n\le f(n)\le(0.2470+o(1))\,n$. In particular $f(n)<n/4$ for all large $n$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:conventions}
All four values $m_1^W$ equal $\alpha^*$, so $m_1$ is unambiguous. Indeed, Proposition~\ref{prop:LR} below gives $m_1^W\le\alpha^*$ for each family, and Section~\ref{sec:transfer} constructs, for discs and for squares, a measurable unit-distance-free $A$ with $\limsup_{r\in\mathbb{N}}|A\cap W_r|/|W_r|\ge\alpha^*$; a limsup over $r\in\mathbb{R}$ is at least the limsup over $r\in\mathbb{N}$. The Lean formalization (Section~\ref{sec:lean}) covers two of the four conventions, squares with $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and discs with $r\in\mathbb{R}$; the other two are covered by the argument above.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:conv}
$f(n)\ge\alpha^*n$ for every $n$, and $f(n)/n\to\alpha^*$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
If $|P|=n$ then $\alpha(P)\ge\alpha^*n$ by definition; hence $f(n)\ge\alpha^*n$.
Fix a finite $P_0$ with $|P_0|=s$ and $\alpha(P_0)=a$. For $N\ge s$ write $N=ks+r$ with $0\le r<s$. Take $k$ translates of $P_0$ and $r$ single points, placed so that distinct pieces are at distance more than $\operatorname{diam}P_0+2$. The union has $N$ points, its unit-distance graph is the disjoint union of the pieces' graphs, and its independence number is $ka+r$. Hence $f(N)\le ka+r\le Na/s+s$, so $\limsup_Nf(N)/N\le a/s$. Taking the infimum over $P_0$ gives $\limsup_Nf(N)/N\le\alpha^*$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:LR}
Let $A$ be measurable and unit-distance-free, and let $W$ be any of the four families. Then $\alpha(P)\ge\bar\delta_W(A)\,|P|$ for every finite nonempty $P$. Hence $m_1^W\le\alpha^*$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $P=\{p_1,\dots,p_n\}$, $\rho=\max_j|p_j|$, $\delta=\bar\delta_W(A)$. For each $x$, $(P+x)\cap A$ is an independent set of $G_{P+x}\cong G_P$, so $|(P+x)\cap A|\le\alpha(P)$. By Tonelli,
\[
  \alpha(P)\,|W_r|\ \ge\ \int_{W_r}|(P+x)\cap A|\,dx=\sum_{j=1}^n|A\cap(W_r+p_j)|\ \ge\ n|A\cap W_r|-\sum_{j=1}^n|W_r\setminus(W_r+p_j)|.
\]
For a disc, $W_r\setminus(W_r+p)$ lies in the annulus $\max(0,r-|p|)\le|x|\le r$, of area $\pi r^2-\pi\max(0,r-|p|)^2\le2\pi r|p|$; for a square it lies in two strips of total area at most $2r(|p_1|+|p_2|)\le2\sqrt2\,r|p|$. In both cases $|W_r\setminus(W_r+p)|\le2\pi r|p|$ and $|W_r|\ge\pi r^2$, so $\alpha(P)\ge n|A\cap W_r|/|W_r|-2n\rho/r$. Letting $r\to\infty$ along a sequence realizing the limsup gives $\alpha(P)\ge n\delta$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:rigidity}
Every $K$-invariant Borel probability measure $\nu$ on $D$ with $\nu(C)=0$ is Haar measure. Equivalently \textup{(}by uniqueness of Fourier coefficients on $D$\textup{)}, $\int_D\psi_z\,d\nu=0$ for all $z\in E\setminus\{0\}$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:cont}
Let $E$ act by measure-preserving maps on a standard probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, with Koopman operators $T_z$ on $L^2(\mu)$. Let $\mathcal{H}_c=\{v\in L^2(\mu):\|T_zv-v\|_2\to0\text{ as }z\to0,\ z\in E\}$, the limit in the topology of $\mathbb{C}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\mathcal{H}_c=L^2(\Omega,\mathcal{F}_c,\mu)$ for a sub-$\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{F}_c$, so the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal{H}_c$ is $\mathbb{E}(\cdot\mid\mathcal{F}_c)$;
\item $\mathcal{H}_c$ is the range of the spectral projection of $\{T_z\}$ on $C$;
\item the restrictions $T_z|_{\mathcal{H}_c}$ extend to a strongly continuous unitary representation $(T_x)_{x\in\mathbb{R}^2}$ on $\mathcal{H}_c$ preserving the cone of nonnegative functions and fixing $\mathbf 1$;
\item if unitaries $V_u$ \textup{(}$u\in K$\textup{)} satisfy $V_uT_zV_u^{-1}=T_{uz}$, then $V_u\mathcal{H}_c=\mathcal{H}_c$ and $V_u$ commutes with the projection onto $\mathcal{H}_c$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:inv}
There is a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$, invariant under all $s_z$ and $\rho_u$, with $\mu(\{\omega:0\in\omega\})\ge\alpha^*$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
The space $\mathcal P(\Omega)$ of Borel probability measures is weak-$*$ compact and metrizable (Riesz--Markov and Banach--Alaoglu), and for a homeomorphism $g$ of $\Omega$ the map $\nu\mapsto g_*\nu$ is weak-$*$ continuous. The set $\{0\in\omega\}$ is clopen, so $\nu\mapsto\nu(0\in\omega)$ is weak-$*$ continuous.

\emph{Translations.} Each $F_N$ is a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$; choose a maximum independent set $J_N\subset F_N$, so $|J_N|\ge\alpha^*|F_N|$ and $J_N-z\in\Omega$ for all $z$. Let $\nu_N=|F_N|^{-1}\sum_{z\in F_N}\delta_{J_N-z}$. Then $\nu_N(0\in\omega)=|J_N|/|F_N|\ge\alpha^*$ and $\|(s_w)_*\nu_N-\nu_N\|_{\rm TV}\le|F_N\triangle(F_N+w)|/|F_N|\to0$. Any weak-$*$ limit point $\mu_0$ is therefore $s_w$-invariant for every $w$ and satisfies $\mu_0(0\in\omega)\ge\alpha^*$.

\emph{Rotations.} Let $G_M$ be Følner sets in $K$ and $\mu_M=|G_M|^{-1}\sum_{u\in G_M}(\rho_u)_*\mu_0$. Each $(\rho_u)_*\mu_0$ is translation invariant, because $(s_w)_*(\rho_u)_*\mu_0=(\rho_u)_*(s_{u^{-1}w})_*\mu_0=(\rho_u)_*\mu_0$; and $(\rho_u)_*\mu_0(0\in\omega)=\mu_0(0\in\omega)$ since $0\in u\omega\iff0\in\omega$. A weak-$*$ limit point $\mu$ of $(\mu_M)$ is translation invariant, rotation invariant by the Følner property, and has $\mu(0\in\omega)\ge\alpha^*$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:weights}
In~\cite[Prop.~4.2]{OAI} a single colouring is averaged over Følner sets of $E\rtimes K$. Applied to a fixed maximum independent set $J$ of a finite set and a finite averaging set $\Phi\subset E\rtimes K$, the empirical measure $\nu_\Phi=|\Phi|^{-1}\sum_{g\in\Phi}\delta_{gJ}$ has $\nu_\Phi(0\in\omega)=\sum_wc(w)\mathbf 1_J(w)/\sum_wc(w)$ with multiplicities $c(w)=\#\{g\in\Phi:g^{-1}0=w\}$ that are not constant in $w$, i.e.\ the $c$-weighted proportion of $J$, for which no lower bound $\alpha^*$ is available a priori. Averaging first over translations (where each position is counted once) and then over rotations (which fix $0$) avoids this.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:field}
Let $x\mapsto v_x$ be a continuous map from $\mathbb{R}^2$ to the real Hilbert space $L^2(\mu;\mathbb{R})$. There is a jointly measurable $H:\mathbb{R}^2\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ with $H(x,\cdot)=v_x$ $\mu$-a.e.\ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^2$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Fix a dense sequence $(x_k)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and a representative of each $v_{x_k}$. For $j\ge1$ let $k_j(x)$ be the least $k$ with $\|v_{x_k}-v_x\|_2<2^{-j}$; it exists by continuity and density, and $x\mapsto k_j(x)$ is Borel because each $x\mapsto\|v_{x_k}-v_x\|_2$ is continuous. Put $H_j(x,\omega)=v_{x_{k_j(x)}}(\omega)=\sum_k\mathbf 1[k_j(x)=k]\,v_{x_k}(\omega)$, which is jointly measurable as a countable sum of products of measurable functions. For fixed $x$, $\sum_j\|H_j(x,\cdot)-v_x\|_1\le\sum_j\|H_j(x,\cdot)-v_x\|_2<\sum_j2^{-j}<\infty$ ($\mu$ is a probability measure), so by Tonelli $\sum_j|H_j(x,\cdot)-v_x|<\infty$ a.e., and $H_j(x,\cdot)\to v_x$ a.e. Let $H=\limsup_jH_j$ where finite and $0$ elsewhere.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:dp}
$A$ contains no two points at distance $1$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Suppose $x,\,y=x+u\in A$ with $|u|=1$. For $0<\eta<1$ let $x'$ be uniform on $B(x,\eta)$ and, independently, $u'$ uniform on the arc $\{e^{i\theta}u:|\theta|<\eta/2\}$, so $|u'-u|<\eta$. Then $\mathbb{P}(x'\notin A_0)=|B(x,\eta)\setminus A_0|/|B(x,\eta)|\to0$. Given $u'$, $x'+u'$ is uniform on $B(x+u',\eta)\subset B(y,2\eta)$, so $\mathbb{P}(x'+u'\notin A_0)\le|B(y,2\eta)\setminus A_0|/(\pi\eta^2)=4|B(y,2\eta)\setminus A_0|/|B(y,2\eta)|\to0$. So for small $\eta$, $\mathbb{P}(x'\in A_0,\ x'+u'\in A_0)>0$. The law of $(x',u')$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $dx\otimes\sigma$ and is supported in $B(0,r)\times S^1$ for an integer $r>|x|+1$. Hence the set $\{(x',u'):x'\in A_0,\ x'+u'\in A_0\}\cap(B(0,r)\times S^1)$ has positive $dx\otimes\sigma$-measure, contradicting $\int_{B(0,r)}\int_{S^1}\mathbf 1_{A_0}(x)\mathbf 1_{A_0}(x+u)\,d\sigma\,dx=0$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
